### What is a RACI Chart?

A RACI chart (or matrix) maps out project tasks against team roles to prevent confusion and overlapping duties.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXXRCCbQ8hXECE0HQMN2fkrJTenewiq52g5e8lcuhXxIWt6JRAfbHo1e1Q8W6ezjv6GuZUsmHbjVQ337pfDDJ_tom8PzbKzj_Z3eUMEYP0_Vz1ijRIx_FqNkdkXdhDwvp-Np7_RzIw9bwg7nzMi4WZzcJGl8RiSmiwHqkM)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXHjL6ZP6cbh39ncZusVUrnojoudbH2m82oa17B6ZKJtkMm1jQJuNGYswHqkJ6zKqof82wybHuNDAVtxktRQapoJH-0IDZtzuR7aRkaovmIvrRpvEHpA09J2rKCD3W_Hwy)

The acronym stands for:

- **R — Responsible:** The person who actually does the work to complete the task.
- **A — Accountable:** The single person who has final approval and owns the outcome (only one "A" per task).
- **C — Consulted:** Subject-matter experts whose input is needed before or during the work.
- **I — Informed:** People who need updates on progress after decisions or steps are completed.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TZzjNemlrXk&t=19)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXevIfxpsF7uF5b0aG2g0Pw2sxS-l-5YsyjVftTZaPJMdYN2Gk51c9kFt0ratT0iTCWl3Sqx8y_ID8QxIYDEx5ZD4UajkVwkVzkwZFUm1MXcph1Qhh0EvHHb0l1hrD1og)
